label: Chest
description: An old iron-bound chest with a stubborn latch.

label: Fire Barrel
description: An oil-soaked barrel with blackened bands.

label: The Great Oak
description: Oakrun's ancient meeting tree, broad enough to shade the crossroads.

label: Covered Carriage
description: A road-worn carriage drawn up beside the Oakrun yard.

label: The Mudwheel
description: A narrow freight wagon rebuilt above tall flood wheels. Name-tablets ride under waxed canvas; a black-shuttered route lamp stays dark while the eastern service is closed.
details: Cargo rule: names and people before freight

label: Stone Well
description: A communal well built from honey-coloured local stone.

label: Noticeboard
description: Oakrun's notices, work offers, and rumours share the same warped boards.

label: Hitching Post
description: A sturdy rail polished smooth by reins and restless horses.

label: Yard Stores
description: Crates and barrels stacked for the next northbound caravan.

label: Broken Waystone
description: A road marker split cleanly through an old crown-and-wheel carving. The newer mileage marks point toward Oakrun; an older arrow underneath points east.

label: Cider Press
description: A broad oak press darkened by years of apple juice. One side has been scrubbed hard enough to raise the grain.
details: Stain beneath the tray: black, not red

label: Ruined Wheelhouse
description: The mill wheel is intact, but every wooden tooth facing upstream has been removed and burned.
details: Ash: mixed with coarse black silt

label: Wayside Shrine
description: A little shelter for travellers' candles. Three saints have names; the fourth face has been worn smooth by deliberate touch.

label: Abandoned Tollhouse
description: The roof has fallen inward, leaving the payment window and its iron grille standing like a rib cage.
details: Doorframe: seven tally cuts, then none

label: Empty Ledger Hook
description: A chain where the toll ledger should hang. The final link was opened with a narrow tool, not broken.

label: Crowned Barrow Stone
description: A grave-slab older than Oakrun bears a small crowned figure lowering a red-painted vessel into the earth.
details: Inscription: payment without a named debtor

label: Unsettled Grave
description: The marker names a local family, but the earth was turned from below and pressed back by careful hands.

label: Severed Apparatus
description: Copper tubes and leather restraints surround a stone basin. Every maker's plate has been pried away, leaving identical four-rivet scars.

label: Blackened Cistern
description: Rainwater inside reflects no sky. A crust around the rim resembles burned sugar until it shifts against the wind.

label: Unnamed Carriage Waystop
description: A painted post, a bell, and enough hard ground for a carriage to turn. The name-board is blank.

label: Quay Lantern Mast
description: A ship's mast planted in the paving and crowded with storm lanterns. Each flame is hooded toward the water.
details: Lowest lantern: marked with arrival dates

label: Black-Reed Brazier
description: Wet reeds burn without smoke inside a shallow copper bowl. Market folk warm their hands without meeting one another's eyes.

label: The Unfinished Ledger
description: A public stone ledger lists every acknowledged disaster in Drazna. Fresh blank pages have already been bolted beneath the old ones.

label: Memorial of the First Record
description: Names from the first verified public account are cut shallowly into black glass. The inscription insists this was the first record, not necessarily the beginning.
details: Final name: removed and recut three times

discovery.title: The First Verified Public Record
discovery.summary: Drazna's black-glass memorial dates the oldest verified public record of the rot. Its own inscription distinguishes the first record from an unknown beginning.

label: The Hollow Bell Tree
description: Hundreds of clappers hang from a dead tree, but there are no bells. In a strong wind they strike nothing and still make a sound.

label: Reliquary of Unrung Bells
description: A locked glass case holds bells retired before they sounded an ill omen. Several have damp mud inside.
details: Count: one greater than the ledger

label: Reed Prayer Wheel
description: A wheel woven from river reeds turns under its own weight, carrying small petitions down into the earth.

label: Candle-Eaten Mile Stone
description: Travelers have melted so many candles over this marker that the road name is preserved only as a hollow in the wax.

label: Drowned Road Bell
description: A bronze bell lies half buried where no tower ever stood. Water beads inside it even in dry weather.
details: Inscription: a destination absent from maps

label: The Rope Throne
description: Snapped bridge ropes have been woven into a high-backed chair overlooking the ravine. Someone repairs it after every storm.

label: Cairn of Borrowed Badges
description: A low cairn carries military badges from both sides of a forgotten battle, pinned together without rank.

label: Root-Bound Mirror
description: Black roots hold a sheet of dull glass upright between the trees. It reflects the road but omits the viewer.

label: Free-Standing Reed Door
description: A door of woven reeds stands alone in knee-deep mud. Its dry handle has been turned recently.
details: Beyond: the same marsh, slightly darker

label: The Blank Grave
description: One grave has a polished marker and no name. Travelers have left notes asking it not to learn theirs.

label: The Last Manifest
description: A brass cargo manifest is nailed to a wrecked wagon. Every passenger arrived; none of the cargo did.

label: Lantern Ferry
description: A narrow black-timber skiff rests on rollers above the quay. Six hooded lanterns can be shuttered independently to signal routes across unsafe water.
details: Hull: patched with three kinds of wood
Lowest plank: glass-black at the nail heads

label: Amber Quay Stall
description: Eel smoke, blackbread, lamp oil, and small necessities fill a stall built to be packed before the water rises.
details: Price board: rewritten after every carriage

label: Teo's Salvage Counter
description: Stamped crates form a counter where Teo buys portable salvage without asking which drowned threshold released it.

label: Crown Sluice Wheel
description: A two-handed iron wheel controls a lower floodgate through chains hidden in the wall. Old red wax remains packed into one spoke.

label: Public Name Rack
description: Bone-white tablets hang in household order. Several families continue across a gap where the hooks were filed away.

label: Roofwright Scaffold
description: A braced scaffold turns three failing roofs into one traversable workshop. Every joint carries Pava Mirek's seven-fold mark.

label: Mud Crown Crane
description: A timber crane lifts furniture, drowned masonry, and sometimes people from the streets below. Claim tags crowd its chain like scales.

label: Low Lantern Cache
description: A tarred reed chest bears no lock, only three shallow wick marks. Its false bottom is cleaner than its ordinary contents.

label: Floodline Memorial
description: A silver rule marks successive flood heights beside names scratched by residents before official cutters arrived.
details: Names below it: later plastered over

label: Wheel-Wash Trough
description: Carriage wheels are scrubbed here before climbing from the quay. Ordinary mud clouds the lye; certain black grains remain sharp and separate.
details: Drain: diverted away from market wells

label: Bundles of Returning Names
description: Letters, household lists, and forwarding addresses are wrapped by destination so absence will not be entered as death.

label: False-Bottom Manifest
description: The public cargo list records lamp oil. A second sheet underneath lists passengers by childhood nickname and the roofs where they can hide.

discovery.title: Passengers Beneath the Cargo
discovery.summary: A genuine Crown seal covers a second manifest that moves people under childhood nicknames. Halfway down, another hand begins choosing the hiding roofs.

label: Omitted Household Tablets
description: Unfinished tablets preserve names absent from the public flood count. Their dates precede the First Scar proclamation without explaining the older damage.
details: Sources: household rolls, not one witness

discovery.title: The Omitted Households
discovery.summary: Two hundred and seventeen household names were prepared for a supplemental flood roll and never hung in the House of Names. Five belonged to the Gate Seven closure shift.

label: The Sealed Flood Order
description: A water-stiff royal order commands Gate Seven closed while occupied roofs remained below it. The text concerns structural collapse, not the origin of the rot.

discovery.title: The Corrected Closure Hour
discovery.summary: The Crown's order sealed Gate Seven after occupied roofs had dropped below its safe line. Its hour was corrected only after the wax hardened.

label: Pre-Proclamation Gauge Roll
description: Maintenance entries describe isolated black silt years before Drazna named a common disaster. The first lines say the material was already present.

discovery.title: Before the Public Record
discovery.summary: Authenticated gauge entries describe isolated black silt before Drazna's verified proclamation. They say it was already present, but not where it came from.

label: Bargemen's Scar Plaque
description: Quay families blame an unregistered salt barge for the First Scar. The arrival date is precise; the vessel name was recut long afterward.

discovery.title: The Nameless Salt Barge
discovery.summary: Quay testimony gives an exact arrival day for a salt barge blamed for the Scar, but its vessel name was recut later and no cargo tally survives.

label: Red-Glass Drain Grating
description: A palace drain carries dark residue toward the old ward. Low Lantern guides call it proof; floodwardens note that floodwater can reverse the same channel.

discovery.title: A Drain That Points Both Ways
discovery.summary: Court-made red glass and black residue share the palace drain, but its scouring marks prove that floodwater has run through it in both directions.

label: Vasko's Cut Rope
description: A diver's line ends in a clean knife cut above a fresh chalk arrow leading away from the official dry route.

discovery.title: Vasko Cut His Own Line
discovery.summary: The Mirek knots are intact below a clean knife cut, there is no blood, and a fresh arrow points away from the official dry route.

label: Six Dry Bunks
description: Six sleeping places occupy the upper dry dock. Two have drag slings fixed beside them for people no longer able to climb.

discovery.title: Six Bunks Above the Water
discovery.summary: Someone has recently fed six people in the old dry dock. Two bunks have drag slings, suggesting survivors who cannot climb home unaided.

label: Three-Knock Wall
description: Three marks repeat along the service wall at shoulder height, then continue where the passage drops beneath still water.
details: Answering scratches: from the far side

discovery.title: An Answer Beyond the Wall
discovery.summary: Fresh three-knock marks continue below the current waterline. A second set of scratches answers from the sealed side.

label: Overwritten Dry-Line
description: White, red, and yellow guide marks disagree about which stones remain above water. Yesterday's safest color ends at a collapsed roof.

discovery.title: Three Routes, No Safe Color
discovery.summary: Crown white, Low Lantern red, and salvage yellow overwrite one another. The most recent official dry line ends under a collapsed roof.

label: Floodwarden Listening Pipe
description: A brass pipe carries the groan of the lower gates upward. Between chain strikes, something below repeats work-call rhythms.

discovery.title: The Third Bell Cadence
discovery.summary: Between the gate's chain blows, the listening pipe repeats a fourteen-beat floodwarden work call. The last five answers are almost buried by pressure noise.

label: Gate Seven Chain Drum
description: The old drum is wound with chain, uniform cloth, and glass-black growth. A human hand remains fixed around the emergency pawl.

label: Roofline Nursery
description: A child's bed is chained above the old floor beside height marks that continue after the official evacuation date.
details: Last height mark: six months after closure

discovery.title: Height Marks After Evacuation
discovery.summary: A child's height marks continue for six months after the official evacuation date. The household name was later removed.

label: Abandoned Warden Tools
description: A complete shift's tools lie in issue order as if their owners expected to return after the gate closed.

discovery.title: Fourteen Tools, Nine Memorials
discovery.summary: Gate Seven's issue rack accounts for fourteen closure workers. The public memorial names only nine.

label: Lower Pressure Gauge
description: The needle taps beyond its painted safe arc whenever the High Crown drains. Someone has added a second scale in charcoal for the Walking Ward.

discovery.title: The Walking Ward Scale
discovery.summary: A charcoal scale beside the official pressure marks protects the Walking Ward foundations instead of palace height. Its safe notch contradicts the sealed Crown order.

label: Third Bell Key Hook
description: A black iron sluice key hangs beside Gate Seven's closure chest. Fourteen shallow notches cross its bow, and no surviving lock is admitted to fit it.
details: Name used below: Odran's Black Key

discovery.title: Odran's Black Key
discovery.summary: A fourteen-notched sluice key was kept beside the closure chest. It marks authority over Gate Seven, but no surviving record identifies the lock it opened.
